coverage.waiver_proof: Offsets 409..502 (45 instruction starts) form the block that follows the BCS at offset 407 when it is NOT taken. Offset 406 is PLP, which pops the status byte pushed by the PHP at offset 248 (the first instruction of the second-probe block C1:BAE2); between 248 and 406 the stack is balanced (PHA at 343 / PLA at 357 are both 16 bit, the call at 398 is JSR C1BC37 which returns normally) and nothing writes the saved byte, so the PLP restores the carry that the PHP saw. Offset 248 has four predecessors in the static CFG: BRL at 181, JSR at 536 and JSR at 564, each immediately preceded by SEC (offsets 180, 535, 563; no instruction in between touches C), so they enter with C = 1; and BRL at 516 (CLC; BRL), which enters with C = 0. Offset 516 lies in the block 505..520, whose first instruction C1:BBE3 has no predecessor inside the routine (no branch targets it and the BRL at 502 does not fall through): it is a separate entry point, reached only by the JSR at C1:B9E6 in the routine C1B93E (tools/decomp_c/captures_r5/refscan.py C1B9EA 505 521). A differential run of C1B9EA starts at the routine entry C1:B9EA, from where block 505..520 cannot be entered (the only code that is jumped to from the 0..504 part is inside the routine or an external callee that returns normally). So on every execution that starts at C1:B9EA C = 1 at the PLP, the BCS at offset 407 is always taken to offset 415, and offset 409 (its fall-through) and everything only reachable from it cannot run: the branch targets 413, 417, 441, 445, 462, 477 and 490 all lie inside the block, and its exits are BRL B9EA at 438 and BRL BBFB at 459/474/487/502.
